title: Source is the query side's read-only array and construction keeps a concrete Scratch
body:
`Buffer<W>` in `buffer.rs` has two halves. One is a read-only array: `open`, `len`, `get`, `range`, which `TypedSuffixArray` holds for its text and suffix array and the search reads. The other is an append buffer: `empty`, `extend_from_slice`, `flush`, with a pending tail and a temp file inside `Disk`. Only `partition` grows anything; every other use in the build makes an array from a finished `Vec` or reads one whole. The build functions are generic over the storage for that one reason.

## Proposal

The trait is `Source<W>` in `source.rs`, with `open`, `len`, `get` and `range` and nothing else, implemented by `MemorySource<W>` over a `Vec` and `DiskSource<W>` over a region of a file. `TypedSuffixArray<W, T: Source<u8>, S: Source<W>>` is the only user.

Construction keeps its own concrete type: `Scratch<W>` in `build/scratch.rs`, the enum of `Memory(Vec)` and `Disk(DiskScratch)` that the build had before `sufr-cad4f6`, chosen by `ScratchKind` from `with_memory_scratch` at runtime and read back with `consume`. `partition`, `sort_partitions`, `write` and `construct` are generic over `W` only, and the kind is passed down as an argument. Nothing under `build/` names `Source`.

`build_to_file` is the one way to build and returns `()`.

## Rejected

- A second trait for the append side that finishes into a `Source`. Jack wants fewer traits, and the append side has one caller.
- The in-memory build from `sufr-7ca2fd`. Jack reverted the builder to writing a file only on 2026-11-04.

## Cost

- `partition` and `sort_partition` change, so the build is benchmarked before and after.
- The `typed` feature exports `Source`, `MemorySource`, `DiskSource` in place of `Buffer`, `Memory`, `Disk`.
